cause.label: equity_offering
cause.what_happened: At 16:01 ET on 2026-09-22 an 8-K moved BMF-650 Phase I (GLP-131) topline from Q3 2026 to October 2026. At 16:05 ET the company launched an unsized underwritten offering of common stock and pre-funded warrants through a single small underwriter (Konik Capital / T.R. Winston), and the stock fell about 19% after hours. At 07:03 ET on 2026-09-23 it terminated the offering with no securities sold, saying market conditions were not conducive, and the stock held the after-hours level through the session.

positioning_check: Short interest was 11,949,049 shares at the 2026-08-31 settlement, up 21.7% from 9,820,656 on 08-14, with 4.96 days to cover. That is about 16.5% of the 72,483,852 shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (prelim 424B5). Source: https://api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/BMEA/short-interest?assetclass=stocks. FINRA publishes about eight business days after settlement, so the position carried into the 09-22 launch and the 09-23 fall cannot be seen. findings.finding: The failed marketed deal leaves the financing need open (cash $35.2M at 06-30, going-concern language in the 10-K), while a Piper Sandler ATM with about $95M of unused capacity sits on an effective S-3 (333-289262) that was used as recently as 09-22. The issuer has drawn this ATM before, so sales or a replacement registered direct can hit on 2026-09-24.
findings.mechanism_in_window: An ATM can sell into any session, 2026-09-24 included. The pulled deal carried no lock-up, because it never closed, so nothing contractual stops a draw or a replacement deal (a registered direct or PIPE) announced before the 09-24 open. A company that launched a deal overnight has already shown it wants cash now and not at the October readout.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's comparable falls on 2025-06-18 (-34.1%, next close -5.24%) and 2025-10-07 (-30.9%, next close -8.94%) line up with priced offerings (the 2025-06-17 pricing release on seekingalpha and the 2025-10-06/07 424B5s and 8-K Item 1.01), so this name has continued after dilution that was actually executed. This time nothing has been executed yet.
findings.why_not_priced: The session priced the termination as a failed financing: it held the after-hours level through a 07:03 cancellation. What it cannot price is a draw or a replacement deal that is not yet announced. Had the tape expected a registered direct at a discount tomorrow, the price would sit nearer a typical discount (10-20% below spot) rather than at the level the market-offering launch set. Had it expected no further supply, the 07:03 cancellation should have lifted it back toward $1.71, and it did not.
findings.independence: The termination release (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/23/3367361/0/en/biomea-fusion-announces-termination-of-proposed-public-offering-of-securities.html) confirms the same S-3 is effective and that no securities were sold. The going-concern text is in the 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1840439/000119312526121825/bmea-20251231.htm, baseline text probe). Both are the issuer's own documents, so this is not fully independent.

The idea that shorts who sold after hours into an expected allocation must now cover is plausible but not countable, because the FINRA data stops at 08-31, so I dropped it rather than sized it.
